Subject: Sudden spike in latency + 5xxs impacting workflows

Jonas —

We're seeing a sharp regression in production this morning that started ~08:40 PDT. Key customer flows (patient summary generation) are timing out or returning 5xx; our telemetry shows: 

- p50: 220ms -> 560ms (2.5x)
- p95: 880ms -> 2.8s (3.2x)
- error rate (5xx) went from 0.4% to 6.9% in the 30m window

This is affecting running jobs for 3 hospitals and causes timeouts in our downstream ingestion. We've exported a small sample of traces and token-level latencies, attached as latency_2026-06-15.csv and a zipped error dump.

We need this triaged immediately — can you confirm receipt and next steps? SLA implications are material; our ops and legal teams are watching.

Thanks,
Samir

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@NimbusHealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in latency + 5xxs impacting workflows (initial findings)

Jonas / Samir — initial triage notes from the infra team (summarized):

Observations:
- Origin: surge on a set of high-cardinality prefixes used by Nimbus for long-context summaries.
- Symptom: head-of-line (HOL) blocking in the batcher due to an aggressive prefetch + long-response tails from large prompt generations. Batching windows are queuing heterogeneous requests behind long-running KV fetches.
- KV behavior: rapid eviction cycles on the prefix store (hot-key thrash) — cache hit rate for the affected tenants dropped from ~92% to ~37% around 08:32. This drove an increase in backend fetches and IO wait.
- Secondary effect: queue buildup triggered token-timeout retries, which amplified the prefetch pressure (feedback loop).

Immediate mitigation (what we did in the last 30m):
- Reduced "hot_lane_prefetch" from aggressive -> conservative for tenant "Nimbus Health" only.
- Narrowed batching window (max batch wait) for that pool from 20ms -> 8ms.
- Temporarily increased KV cache allocation on the host nodes serving Nimbus (bumped reserved slots + prevented eviction of pinned prefixes).

Impact of mitigations so far:
- p95 down from 2.8s to ~1.1s in the last 10 minutes
- Error rate decreased to ~1.2% (still above baseline)

Next steps (engineering):
- Run a targeted prefetch throttle rollout (gradual) and monitor miss-rate / request tails.
- Add short-term pinning for the top-20 Nimbus prefixes (requested from Nimbus sample).
- Open a deep-dive ticket to examine the batching heuristics that allow long-tail requests to block heterogeneous batches (owner: karthik_iyer).

I'll prepare a technical memo with timeline and logs. Attaching a snapshot: ops_snapshot-2026-06-15.png.

Laura Bennett
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachments: ops_snapshot-2026-06-15.png (PNG)

- Affected customers: 3 hospital clusters (production) — latency and 5xxs degraded between 08:30–09:05 PDT.
- Business impact: real user transactions retried or failed; Nimbus has paused two downstream jobs. Legal/ops are flagging SLA exposure.
- Current status: mitigations reduced p95 to ~1.1s but not fully back to baseline.

Request / proposed actions: 
1) Approve a one-month service credit for Nimbus proportional to incident window (we estimate 4–6 hours of impact). Sales/CS to finalize wording.
2) Approve emergency allocation of 2 additional Dedicated nodes (48 GPU hours) to reduce noise from multi-tenant interference while we fix policy.
3) Priority assignment: karthik_iyer + laura_bennett to lead a 72-hour remediation plan to: 
   - adjust batching policy and implement HOL-protection heuristics,
   - introduce prefix pinning and eviction smoothing,
   - add synthetic load-test covering high-cardinality prefix cases.

Samir — we will keep you closely updated. We expect to have a full remediation timeline by EOD plus an interim hours-based credit proposal for legal.

Marissa Cole
